chapters.title: Chapter 3: What Sits on Top of the Slabs

lessons.title: Surcharge, Marginal Relief for High Earners and the 4% Cess

body.text: The slab table stops at 30%, but the true top rate does not. Surcharge adds a percentage of your tax once income crosses ₹50 lakh, and 4% cess sits on top of everything, taking the highest new regime marginal rate to 39%.

markDefs.definition: An additional tax charged as a percentage of income tax, not of income, for taxpayers whose income crosses specified thresholds.
The Health and Education Cess: 4% of income tax plus surcharge, payable by every taxpayer who has any tax to pay.

children.text: After the slabs and the rebate, two final layers complete the tax bill.
affects everyone who pays any tax at all. Both are calculated on tax, not on income, which is the single most important thing to remember about them.

body.caption: Surcharge on Income Tax, Individuals, Tax Year 2026-27

children.text: Unlike slab rates, surcharge rates are not graduated. Once Total Income crosses a threshold, the higher surcharge rate applies to your entire income tax, not just to the tax on income above the threshold. That design creates cliffs, which is why a second form of marginal relief exists for high earners. Like the old regime slab rates, surcharge rates are prescribed in the annual Finance Act.

body.text: Surcharge on tax attributable to dividends and to capital gains on listed shares and equity mutual funds is capped at 15%, even when Total Income crosses ₹2 crore or ₹5 crore. This is one reason very high earners with large equity gains pay a lower overall rate on those gains than on salary. Chapter 4 covers special-rate income in detail.

body.caption: The rebate applies only up to ₹12 lakh (new regime) and surcharge only above ₹50 lakh, so in practice a taxpayer uses one or the other, never both

children.text: Because surcharge and cess multiply the 30% slab rate, the tax on each extra rupee rises in steps as income crosses each threshold.

body.title: Marginal Rate on Slab-Rate Income, Including Surcharge and Cess

body.label: Highest Marginal Rates in India
body.context: 30% × 1.25 × 1.04 = 39%. 30% × 1.37 × 1.04 = 42.744%. The 25% surcharge cap is one of the strongest reasons crorepati taxpayers choose the new regime.

children.text: At exactly ₹50,00,000 of Total Income, new regime tax is ₹10,80,000 with no surcharge. One rupee more and 10% surcharge applies to the whole tax, adding about ₹1,08,000. To prevent this, the law caps tax plus surcharge: it cannot exceed the tax plus surcharge payable at the threshold, plus the income earned above the threshold.

body.caption: Applies at each surcharge threshold: ₹50 lakh, ₹1 crore, ₹2 crore and, in the old regime, ₹5 crore
Surcharge Marginal Relief Just Above ₹50 Lakh, New Regime

body.title: Show me the math: how wide is each relief zone?

children.text: Relief applies until the extra surcharge triggered at the threshold is used up. Above ₹50 lakh, with E as the excess, tax plus surcharge is 1.10 × (₹10,80,000 + 0.30E) and the cap is ₹10,80,000 + E. They meet when 0.67E = ₹1,08,000, so E ≈ ₹1,61,194. The same method gives zones of about ₹1,96,947 above ₹1 crore, about ₹8,92,800 above ₹2 crore, and, in the old regime only, about ₹30,17,827 above ₹5 crore.

body.caption: Surcharge Marginal Relief Zones, Slab-Rate Income Only

body.text: Just like the rebate relief at ₹12 lakh, cess is added after the surcharge cap. Inside each surcharge relief zone, every extra rupee costs about ₹1.04 of tax, a marginal rate of roughly 104%. A senior executive negotiating a package that lands at ₹51 lakh of Total Income may take home less than at exactly ₹50 lakh.

columns.label: Surcharge
points: Applies only above ₹50 lakh of Total Income
Rate of 10%, 15%, 25% or 37% depending on income
Marginal relief softens the jump at each threshold
Capped at 15% on tax on dividends and equity capital gains

columns.label: Health and Education Cess
points: Applies to every taxpayer with any tax payable
Charged on income tax plus surcharge
Turns a 30% slab into 31.2% for someone below ₹50 lakh

children.text: The cess replaced the earlier 3% education cess in 2018 and has stayed at 4% since. It is small in percentage terms but easy to forget. When your payroll team projects TDS or you estimate advance tax, always multiply tax and surcharge by 1.04 before comparing with what has been deducted.

body.title: Total Tax at ₹80 Lakh
body.prompt: Dr. Menon, a cardiac surgeon at a private hospital in Bengaluru, is on the new regime with Total Income of ₹80,00,000, all taxed at slab rates. What is his total tax payable, including surcharge and cess?
body.explanation: Slab tax: ₹3,00,000 + 30% of ₹56,00,000 = ₹19,80,000. Surcharge at 10%: ₹1,98,000. Income is far above the ₹50 lakh relief zone, so no marginal relief. Tax plus surcharge: ₹21,78,000. Cess at 4%: ₹87,120. Total: ₹22,65,120, an effective rate of about 28.3%.

body.title: Just Over ₹50 Lakh
body.question: Nandini, a partner-track lawyer in Delhi, is on the new regime with Total Income of ₹50,50,000, all slab-rate income. What is her total tax payable, including cess?
options: ₹12,52,680, full tax plus 10% surcharge plus cess
₹11,38,800, tax with no surcharge because the excess is small
body.explanation: Tax is ₹10,95,000 and 10% surcharge is ₹1,09,500, a total of ₹12,04,500. The cap is tax at ₹50 lakh (₹10,80,000) plus the ₹50,000 excess: ₹11,30,000. Marginal relief is ₹74,500. Adding 4% cess to ₹11,30,000 gives ₹11,75,200. Without relief she would have paid ₹12,52,680.

body.title: The New Regime Cap
body.textWithBlank: Under the new regime, the highest surcharge rate for an individual is capped at ___%.
body.explanation: The old regime surcharge goes up to 37% above ₹5 crore. The new regime caps it at 25%, bringing the top marginal rate down from about 42.74% to 39%.

body.title: The Promoter Who Wants the Old Regime
body.scenario: Vikramaditya is the promoter and managing director of a listed auto components company in Pune. His gross salary for tax year 2026-27 is ₹6,00,75,000 and he has no other income. He tells his CA he wants the old regime "because I can claim ₹1.5 lakh under 80C, ₹25,000 for health insurance and ₹2 lakh of home loan interest."
body.prompt: Compare his total tax under both regimes, including surcharge and cess, and advise him.
body.modelAnswer: New regime: Total Income is ₹6,00,75,000 − ₹75,000 standard deduction = ₹6,00,00,000. Slab tax ₹1,75,80,000; surcharge capped at 25%, ₹43,95,000; cess ₹8,79,000. Total: ₹2,28,54,000. Old regime: Total Income is ₹6,00,75,000 − ₹50,000 standard deduction − ₹3,75,000 deductions = ₹5,96,50,000. Slab tax ₹1,77,07,500; surcharge at 37%, ₹65,51,775; cess ₹9,70,371. Total: ₹2,52,29,646. The new regime saves him about ₹23,75,646. His ₹3,75,000 of deductions save tax at around 42.74%, roughly ₹1.6 lakh, which is nowhere near enough to offset the 37% surcharge. He should stay on the new regime.

points: Surcharge is a percentage of income tax: 10% above ₹50 lakh, 15% above ₹1 crore, 25% above ₹2 crore, and 37% above ₹5 crore in the old regime only
The new regime caps surcharge at 25%, so its top marginal rate is 39% against 42.74% in the old regime
Surcharge on tax on dividends and equity capital gains is capped at 15%
Marginal relief ensures tax plus surcharge never rises by more than the income earned above each threshold
The 4% Health and Education Cess is charged on tax plus surcharge for every taxpayer, with no threshold
Inside each relief zone, cess pushes the marginal rate to about 104%

body.text: Surcharge rates, thresholds and relief zones shown are for individuals for tax year 2026-27, assuming only slab-rate income. Special-rate income changes the calculation. Surcharge rates are set in the annual Finance Act and can change in any Budget. This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice.
